plainFields.name: price
plainFields.description: Unit price of the product variant at time of purchase. Stored as snapshot value for historical accuracy.

plainFields.name: total_amount
plainFields.description: Total cost of this order item (quantity × price). Calculated at order creation but stored for performance.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this order item was created. Always set at order placement.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this order item was last updated. Typically same as created_at, as order items are immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Used for audit trails and potential data purging according to retention policy.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_addresses
models.description:
Shipping and billing address details captured at time of order placement, ensuring historical accuracy regardless of later profile changes.

This table stores a snapshot of the customer's address information at the exact moment an order is placed. Even if the customer later updates their profile address, this record remains unchanged to provide an accurate audit trail of what was specified during the purchase transaction.

This is a subsidiary table managed entirely through its parent order entity and does not have independent API endpoints. It serves as a critical component for order fulfillment, legal compliance, and financial auditing.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent order. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

plainFields.name: address_line1
plainFields.description: First line of the street address (e.g., 123 Main Street). Required field.

plainFields.name: address_line2
plainFields.description: Second line of the street address (e.g., Apt 5B, Suite 100). Optional field for apartment or suite numbers.

plainFields.name: city
plainFields.description: City or town name for the address. Required field.

plainFields.name: state
plainFields.description: State, province, or region name for the address. Required for countries with subdivisions.

plainFields.name: postal_code
plainFields.description: Postal or ZIP code for the address. Required field for accurate shipping calculations.

plainFields.name: country
plainFields.description: Country name in full form (e.g., United States, Canada). Required field.

plainFields.name: phone
plainFields.description: Contact phone number for delivery notifications and carrier coordination. Required field.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address for order confirmation and shipping notifications. Required field.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this address snapshot was created (when order was placed). Always set to order creation time.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last update to this address record. Usually same as created_at as addresses are immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp indicating when this record was logically deleted. Never physically removes data to preserve audit trail.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_payments
models.description:
Payment transaction details for orders, capturing method, status, gateway ID, and amount at the time of processing.

Records all payment attempts associated with orders including authorization, capture, refund, and failure states. Each payment record is linked to exactly one order and captures the payment details at the moment of transaction, ensuring historical accuracy even if payment methods are later modified.

Used for financial reconciliation, audit trails, and reporting on payment success rates. Integrates with payment gateways to store transaction IDs and status updates. Supports refund processing through linked shopping_mall_order_refunds table.

Important: This is a primary entity that requires independent management for payment reconciliation workflows and financial reporting across the entire system, not just within each order context.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: The order this payment is associated with. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

plainFields.name: payment_method
plainFields.description: Type of payment method used (credit_card, paypal, bank_transfer, crypto, gift_card).

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current payment status: pending, processing, authorized, captured, declined, refunded, partially_refunded.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: Payment amount in USD, matching the order total at time of payment.

plainFields.name: gateway_id
plainFields.description: Unique transaction ID assigned by the payment gateway (e.g., Stripe, PayPal).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this payment record was initially created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this payment record.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this payment record was logically deleted (soft delete).

models.name: shopping_mall_order_events
models.description:
Immutable audit log of all status changes and key events in order lifecycle, with timestamp and actor context.

Records every state transition in an order's journey, including who initiated the change (customer, seller, admin, or system) and any additional context. Essential for auditing, compliance, customer service investigations, and system analytics.

Each event represents a single point-in-time status change. Events are append-only and never modified after creation. The table supports comprehensive reporting on order lifecycle patterns, delay causes, and resolution times.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: The order this event belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: The new status assigned to the order after this event. Valid values: pending, confirmed, shipped, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, returned, cancelled, refunded.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor who initiated this event. Values: customer, seller, admin, system.

plainFields.name: details
plainFields.description: Additional context about the event, such as reason for cancellation, message from seller, or system-generated notes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this event was created and recorded in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this event record (rarely changed after creation).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete marker for audit trail integrity. If set, indicates this event was logically deleted (very rare).

models.name: shopping_mall_order_returns
models.description:
Customer-initiated return requests for purchased items, tracking status, reason, and linkage to refund processing.

Captures the complete lifecycle of return requests initiated by customers after delivery of goods. Each return is tied to a specific order and may result in a corresponding refund.

Returns remain attached to the original order even if the order data changes, providing complete historical context for dispute resolution. Customers can submit one return request per order, and each request progresses through defined status stages from initiation to completion.

The reason field captures the customer's justification for return, subject to moderation if flagged. Status transitions are tracked with timestamps, and refunds are linked only when processed successfully.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: The order this return request applies to. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the return request. Valid values: requested, approved, rejected, processed, completed.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Customer's detailed explanation for the return request. Must be between 50-2000 characters as defined in requirements.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the return request was initially submitted.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last status change in this return request.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_refunds
models.description:
Records financial refunds issued for returned items or order adjustments.

Tracks the complete lifecycle of refund transactions initiated by customer return requests. Each refund record is directly linked to a specific return request and the parent order, ensuring traceability from return through payout. Refunds are never created independently - they can only be processed through the return workflow. The refund amount reflects the amount authorized for repayment, which may differ from original payment due to restocking fees or partial returns.

Status tracking allows accounting teams to reconcile refunds with bank processing, identify failed or reversed transactions, and generate financial reports.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_return_id
foreignFields.description: The return request that triggered this refund. {@link shopping_mall_order_returns.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: The original order for which this refund was processed. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: The total refund amount in USD. Equals the approved return amount minus any restocking fees.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the refund. Valid values: pending (awaiting processing), processed (successfully paid), failed (payment gateway error), reversed (funds returned to platform).

plainFields.name: refund_method
plainFields.description: The method used to issue the refund. Values: original_payment (reversed to original payment method), store_credit (credited to account), bank_transfer (direct to bank account), check (physical mailed check).

plainFields.name: gateway_reference_id
plainFields.description: The unique identifier assigned by the payment gateway for this refund transaction. Useful for reconciliation and support.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund record was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund record was last updated (e.g., status change).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this refund was logically deleted for audit compliance. Null if still active.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_cancellation_reasons
models.description:
Structured lookup table for predefined reasons why orders are cancelled.

Enables analytics, policy enforcement, and automated workflows by capturing standardized cancellation reasons. Admins can manage this list to control which reasons are available to customers and which trigger specific responses or reviews.

Each cancellation reason is associated with a category that groups similar reasons (e.g., inventory_issue, customer_request, fraud_risk). Reasons can be deactivated by setting active to false without deleting them, preserving audit history. This table is referenced by shopping_mall_orders when an order is cancelled.

This is a primary entity because admins must independently create, update, activate, deactivate, and search cancellation reasons in the administrative dashboard—each reason is a distinct policy control point that does not depend on any order.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The human-readable cancellation reason text presented to customers or used in reports. Must be unique and descriptive.

plainFields.name: category
plainFields.description: Categorization of the cancellation reason (e.g., customer_request, inventory_issue, fraud_risk, pricing_error, duplicate_order). Used for filtering and reporting.

plainFields.name: active
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the cancellation reason is currently active and available for selection. Inactive reasons are preserved for historical reporting.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cancellation reason was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cancellation reason was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cancellation reason was logically deleted (soft delete). Null if still active.

models.name: shopping_mall_delivery_trackings
models.description:
Logs individual delivery status events with timestamps, location data, and carrier-provided updates for each order shipment.

Records every status change in the delivery lifecycle including shipped, in_transit, out_for_delivery, and delivered states. Each record represents a single point-in-time update from the carrier system, capturing tracking number, carrier name, estimated delivery date, actual delivery date, and location data as received directly from shipping providers.

This table is append-only - existing records are never modified or deleted. It serves as the official audit trail for delivery events, enabling customers to track order progress and providing data for analytics on delivery performance.

Records are created automatically by system integrations with FedEx, UPS, DHL, and USPS APIs as delivery status updates are received. All events are linked to their corresponding shopping_mall_orders record via foreign key.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: The order this delivery tracking event belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

plainFields.name: tracking_number
plainFields.description: Unique tracking number assigned by the shipping carrier. This is the primary identifier customers use to track their shipment.

plainFields.name: carrier_name
plainFields.description: Name of the shipping carrier (e.g., 'FedEx', 'UPS', 'DHL', 'USPS') providing the delivery service.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current delivery status of the shipment. Values: 'shipped', 'in_transit', 'out_for_delivery', 'delivered'. Reflects the most recent update from the carrier API.

plainFields.name: estimated_delivery_date
plainFields.description: Date and time when the carrier estimates the package will be delivered, provided by the carrier system.

plainFields.name: actual_delivery_date
plainFields.description: Date and time when the package was actually delivered, as confirmed by the carrier. Null until delivery occurs.

plainFields.name: location
plainFields.description: Geographical location where the status update occurred. Usually the city and state of the most recent scan point.

plainFields.name: package_weight
plainFields.description: Weight of the package in kilograms as reported by the carrier system.

plainFields.name: package_dimensions
plainFields.description: Dimensions of the package as reported by the carrier system, formatted as "length x width x height" units.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this delivery tracking event was recorded in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this delivery tracking event was last modified in the system.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_methods
models.description:
Stores supported payment methods with their configuration, enabled status, and regional availability.

Defines all payment processing options available on the platform including credit cards, digital wallets, bank transfers, and cryptocurrency. Each payment method has unique parameters that control how it functions, which currencies it supports, and which regions it's available in.

Payment methods are managed by administrators through the admin dashboard. When a payment method is enabled, it becomes available for customers to select during checkout. Each payment method can have arbitrary configuration parameters stored as JSON to accommodate different gateway requirements (e.g., Stripe, PayPal, CoinBase).

The enabled flag controls whether customers can use this payment method. The supported_currencies array defines which currencies this payment method can process in the platform's base currency context. The regions field defines geographic restrictions using ISO 3166 country codes.

All payment method modifications are tracked through the deleted_at field for audit compliance.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Display name of the payment method shown to customers (e.g., "Visa", "Apple Pay", "Bank Transfer").

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Classification type of payment method: "credit_card", "digital_wallet", "bank_transfer", "cryptocurrency", "alternative_payment".

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description explaining the payment method's usage, limitations, and any customer instructions.

plainFields.name: enabled
plainFields.description: Whether this payment method is currently available for customers to use during checkout.

plainFields.name: supported_currencies
plainFields.description: JSON array of ISO 4217 currency codes (e.g., ["USD", "EUR", "JPY"]) that this payment method supports.

plainFields.name: regions
plainFields.description: JSON array of ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes (e.g., ["US", "CA", "JP"]) where this payment method is available.

plainFields.name: configuration
plainFields.description: JSON object containing payment method-specific configuration parameters (gateway IDs, API keys, rate limits, etc.).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this payment method was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this payment method was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this payment method was logically deleted (soft delete) for audit trail purposes.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_intents
models.description:
Represents payment authorization requests with unique intent IDs, cart totals, currency, and initial processing state before capture.

This table manages the authorization phase of payment processing, where a customer initiates payment for their cart but the funds are not yet captured. Each intent represents a pending payment transaction that may be captured, declined, or expired. The intent is linked to the specific cart being paid, the chosen payment method, and the customer authorizing the payment. Payment intents are ephemeral objects created during checkout and transition through states: pending → authorized → captured or declined/expired.

Intents are not part of the core order system but serve as the mechanism for external payment gateway authorization. They provide a standardized interface for processing payments while decoupling financial operations from order creation logic. The status field indicates the current lifecycle stage of the payment authorization.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_cart_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the shopping cart being processed for payment. {@link shopping_mall_carts.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_payment_method_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the specific payment method selected for this authorization. {@link shopping_mall_payment_methods.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer who initiated this payment authorization. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: intent_id
plainFields.description: Unique identifier generated by the payment gateway for this authorization request. Used for matching gateway responses and tracking in external systems.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: The currency code for this payment (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY'). Must match the platform's supported currencies.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: The total amount to be authorized in the specified currency. Must be positive and include all cart items, taxes, and shipping charges at time of authorization.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current lifecycle status of this payment intent. Valid values: 'pending' (created but not yet sent to gateway), 'authorized' (gateway has approved the authorization), 'captured' (funds have been successfully settled), 'declined' (gateway rejected authorization), 'expired' (authorization timed out without capture).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this payment intent was first created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this payment intent was last updated (e.g., when status changed).

models.name: shopping_mall_payments
models.description:
Core payment records tracking transaction lifecycle: created, processing, authorized, captured, declined, refunded, or partially refunded status.

Stores individual payment transactions with their financial details and lifecycle status. Each payment is linked to a payment intent that captured the authorization request, and may be associated with a refund if the transaction is reversed. Payment status evolves through various states based on gateway responses and system validations.

This table forms the central record of completed payment operations and is queried independently by users to check payment status, retry failed payments, and view payment history.

The amount and currency are captured at transaction time to preserve historical accuracy regardless of later currency fluctuations. Status changes are tracked in the payment_audit_logs table for audit compliance.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_payment_intent_id
foreignFields.description: Authorization request that initiated this payment. {@link shopping_mall_payment_intents.id}.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: Transaction amount in the specified currency. Captured at time of payment processing to preserve historical accuracy regardless of later currency fluctuations. Always expressed in the payment intent's currency.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: ISO 4217 currency code for this transaction (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY). Matches the currency of the linked payment intent and remains fixed for historical accuracy.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current payment status. Valid values: created, processing, authorized, captured, declined, refunded, partially_refunded. Follows payment workflow: created -> processing -> (authorized -> captured) or declined or voided. Refunded and partially_refunded indicate reversal of captured amount.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this payment record was created in the system, corresponding to the initial payment request.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this payment record was last updated, typically when status changes due to gateway response or system processing.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Used to maintain audit trail compliance while logically removing access to cancelled or invalidated payments. Payments are never permanently deleted.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_refunds
models.description:
Records refund requests initiated for processed payments, including amount, status, and gateway response.

Captures permanent records of money returned to customers after successful payment. Each refund is tied to an original payment transaction and may apply to one or more order items. Refunds are immutable financial records - once issued, their details cannot be changed.

Supports partial refunds (when only part of the payment is returned) and full refunds. The system tracks whether the refund was successfully processed, declined, or is pending. Gateway-specific responses and error codes are stored for reconciliation.

Refunds are never soft-deleted or updated - they form a permanent audit trail of returned funds. Querying by refund status, payment reference, or date range is common for finance reporting and dispute resolution.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_payment_id
foreignFields.description: The original payment transaction being refunded. {@link shopping_mall_payments.id}.

plainFields.name: refund_amount
plainFields.description: The monetary value being refunded, expressed in the transaction's original currency. Must be less than or equal to the original payment amount.

plainFields.name: refund_status
plainFields.description: Current state of this refund request: 'pending', 'succeeded', 'failed', or 'partially_succeeded'. Determines if funds have been returned to customer.

plainFields.name: gateway_response_code
plainFields.description: The raw error or success code returned by the payment gateway during refund processing.

plainFields.name: gateway_response_message
plainFields.description: Human-readable message from the payment gateway about the refund status or reason for failure.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this refund request was created in the system. Never updated - immutable audit record.

plainFields.name: refund_items
plainFields.description: JSON array storing the list of order item IDs and refunded amounts for partial refunds. Example: [{"order_item_id": "uuid", "amount": 25.50}].

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp for audit trail compliance. If null, record is active. If populated, the record has been logically deleted for compliance purposes.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_audit_logs
models.description:
Immutable audit trail of all payment status changes, including timestamp, actor, old/new values, and reason for change.

Records every state transition in the payment processing lifecycle for compliance, forensic analysis, and operational transparency. Each record captures the exact state change that occurred, by which actor, and why it happened.

The table uses a polymorphic actor reference system with actor_type and actor_id to track changes made by customers, sellers, or administrators without nullable fields. The payment_entity_type field identifies which payment entity (payment, intent, refund) was modified, while old_value and new_value store serialized JSON representations of the state before and after the change.

The table follows an append-only pattern - records are never updated or deleted, ensuring complete auditability. Each audit record is automatically generated by the system during payment state transitions, not initiated by direct user interaction.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who initiated the payment state change, if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer involved in the payment state change, if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller involved in the payment state change, if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: payment_intent_id
foreignFields.description: The payment intent that was audited, if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_payment_intents.id}.

foreignFields.name: payment_refund_id
foreignFields.description: The payment refund that was audited, if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_payment_refunds.id}.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor who triggered the audit event (admin, customer, seller, system). Used with actor_id to implement polymorphic ownership without nullable foreign keys.

plainFields.name: payment_entity_type
plainFields.description: Type of payment entity that was modified (payment, intent, refund). This identifies which payment table the foreign key relates to for audit context.

plainFields.name: old_value
plainFields.description: Serialized JSON representation of the payment entity state BEFORE the change occurred. This immutable record captures the exact state that was modified.

plainFields.name: new_value
plainFields.description: Serialized JSON representation of the payment entity state AFTER the change occurred. This immutable record captures the new state that was established.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Business reason for the payment state change. Examples: 'Customer initiated refund', 'Payment gateway declined', 'System auto-retry', 'Admin override'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this audit record was created. This is the point-in-time when the payment state change was captured.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this audit record was last updated. In append-only audit systems, this is typically identical to created_at since records are never modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete marker to maintain audit trail integrity. Even for audit records, the system supports soft delete for compliance and data retention policies without losing historical context.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_gateway_logs
models.description:
Logs all communication with payment gateways including request/response payloads, error codes, response times, and retry attempts.

Captures complete request and response data for every payment gateway interaction to enable troubleshooting, security audits, and compliance verification. Each log entry is tied to a specific payment intent, creating a verifiable audit trail of all gateway communications during payment processing.

The request and response payloads are stored as raw JSON strings to preserve exact gateway interaction details. Error codes capture standardized gateway responses while response_time_ms records performance metrics critical for SLA monitoring. Retry attempts track system recovery behaviors during gateway outages.

This table is purely operational logging and not directly user-managed. It serves as the foundation for payment gateway diagnostics and compliance reporting.

foreignFields.name: payment_intent_id
foreignFields.description: The payment intent that triggered this gateway communication. {@link shopping_mall_payment_intents.id}.

plainFields.name: request_payload
plainFields.description: Raw JSON payload sent to the payment gateway. Stored as string to preserve exact formatting and content for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: response_payload
plainFields.description: Raw JSON response received from the payment gateway. Stored as string to preserve exact formatting and content for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: error_code
plainFields.description: Standardized error code returned by the payment gateway (e.g., 'gateway_timeout', 'insufficient_funds', 'card_declined'). Null when no error occurred.

plainFields.name: response_time_ms
plainFields.description: Response time in milliseconds from gateway request to response receipt. Used for performance monitoring and SLA compliance.

plainFields.name: retry_attempt
plainFields.description: Number of retry attempts made for this gateway communication. First attempt is 0, subsequent retries increment by 1.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this gateway communication log was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this gateway communication log was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Used to maintain audit trail while logically removing records from active views.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_reconciliation
models.description:
Tracks payment reconciliation jobs comparing system records with gateway settlement reports, flagging discrepancies for finance team.

System-generated audit table that records periodic reconciliation tasks between the platform's payment records and external payment gateway settlement reports. Each record represents one reconciliation cycle, capturing the difference between internal ledger balances and external system balances, along with detailed discrepancy information.

Reconciliation jobs are automatically triggered by batch processes and serve as the primary source for financial audits. Finance teams use this data to identify and resolve inconsistencies between the platform's records and payment provider reports, ensuring monetary accuracy and regulatory compliance.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_payment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the payment record being reconciled. {@link shopping_mall_payments.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_payment_gateway_log_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the gateway settlement log record for comparison. {@link shopping_mall_payment_gateway_logs.id}.

plainFields.name: job_id
plainFields.description: Unique identifier for this reconciliation job, generated by the system.

plainFields.name: job_date
plainFields.description: Date and time when the reconciliation job was executed.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current state of the reconciliation job: 'pending', 'in_progress', 'completed', 'failed'.

plainFields.name: total_payments_expected
plainFields.description: Total amount of payments expected from system records.

plainFields.name: total_payments_received
plainFields.description: Total amount reported by the payment gateway for the same period.

plainFields.name: difference_amount
plainFields.description: The monetary difference between expected and received amounts. Positive means system has more than gateway, negative means gateway has more than system.

plainFields.name: discrepancy_count
plainFields.description: Number of individual payment transactions that did not match between systems.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of reconciliation findings, including specific transaction IDs that mismatched and reasons.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reconciliation record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reconciliation record was last updated.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_regions
models.description:
Mapping of permitted payment methods by country and currency to enforce regional restrictions automatically.

This configuration table defines which payment methods are available in specific geographic and monetary jurisdictions. It enforces compliance with regional payment regulations and merchant requirements by restricting available payment options based on the customer's country and transaction currency.

Each record represents a single permitted association between a payment method and a specific country-currency combination. When a customer initiates payment, the system queries this table to filter available payment methods based on their location and transaction currency, ensuring only compliant and supported methods are presented.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_payment_method_id
foreignFields.description: The payment method that is permitted in this region. {@link shopping_mall_payment_methods.id}.

plainFields.name: country_code
plainFields.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., 'US', 'JP', 'BR') where this payment method is enabled.

plainFields.name: currency_code
plainFields.description: ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., 'USD', 'JPY', 'BRL') of transactions where this payment method is permitted.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_gateway_failovers
models.description:
Manages gateway failover configuration and history, tracking primary/secondary/tertiary switches during outages.

Tracks the configuration of payment gateway failover hierarchy and historical failover events to ensure payment processing continuity during provider outages. Maintains the priority order of gateways (primary, secondary, tertiary) and logs the timing and frequency of failover events to support system reliability monitoring and incident analysis.

This is system configuration data accessed during payment processing but not directly manipulated by end users. It's configured by administrators through payment settings and directly referenced by the payment processing engine to determine fallback routing strategies.

plainFields.name: primary_gateway
plainFields.description: The primary payment gateway provider name that is used first for processing payments.

plainFields.name: secondary_gateway
plainFields.description: The secondary payment gateway provider name that is used as backup if the primary fails.

plainFields.name: tertiary_gateway
plainFields.description: The tertiary payment gateway provider name that is used as final backup if both primary and secondary fail.

plainFields.name: last_failover_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent gateway failover event, indicating when the system switched from primary to secondary/tertiary.

plainFields.name: failover_count
plainFields.description: Total number of failover events recorded since configuration was created, tracking system reliability.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this failover configuration was initially created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this failover configuration was last modified or updated.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_tokenizations
models.description:
Securely stores tokenized payment credentials (card, wallet, crypto) linked to users who explicitly consented to save payment methods.

Enables PCI-DSS compliant storage of payment information by replacing sensitive data with tokens. Tokens are generated for customers and sellers who choose to save payment methods, allowing future transactions without re-entering card details. Each token is scoped to a specific actor and can be revoked by deleting the record.

This table does not store raw card numbers, CVVs, or full primary account numbers (PAN) — only masked representations and cryptographic tokens. Data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 with a key managed by the vault system.

Tokens are always accessed through their owning actor context (customer or seller), never independently. This table supports payment method management workflows where users add, remove, or update stored credentials via their account settings.

foreignFields.name: customer_payment_token_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer who owns this payment token. Only populated when actor_type is 'customer'. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_payment_token_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller who owns this payment token. Only populated when actor_type is 'seller'. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor who owns this token. Value is either 'customer' or 'seller'. Determines which foreign key field is populated.

plainFields.name: token_id
plainFields.description: Unique identifier assigned by the payment gateway for the tokenized credential. This is the value returned by the payment processor and used in subsequent transactions.

plainFields.name: token_data
plainFields.description: The actual encrypted token string provided by the gateway. May contain masked card number (e.g., '****-****-****-1234') or wallet identifier. Used for display and partial ID match during payment selection.

plainFields.name: encrypted_key
plainFields.description: The AES-256 encrypted symmetric key used to decrypt the token_data, stored separately for PCI-DSS compliance. Requires key management system to decrypt.

plainFields.name: is_default
plainFields.description: Indicates if this token is the default payment method for the actor. Only one token per actor can be marked as default.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the token was originally created and stored in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the token was last updated (e.g., when marked as default or when metadata changed).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the token was logically deleted (soft delete). Indicates the token is no longer valid. NULL if still active.

plainFields.name: payment_method_type
plainFields.description: Type of payment method represented by this token: 'credit_card', 'debit_card', 'digital_wallet', 'cryptocurrency'. Used for classification and UI display.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_disputes
models.description:
Handles chargeback and fraud disputes with status, evidence, associated transactions, and resolution outcomes.

Tracks formal dispute cases initiated by customers or sellers regarding payment transactions. Each dispute represents a formal challenge to a payment's validity with supporting documentation and a clear resolution path.

Disputes can be initiated by customers (claiming unauthorized charge, incorrect amount) or sellers (claiming goods were delivered). Each dispute is linked to a specific payment and may be assigned to an admin for investigation.

The system maintains an audit trail of all dispute actions and preserves evidence as referenced files or document links. Disputes progress through defined statuses (open, under_review, resolved, cancelled) with final outcomes recorded for financial reconciliation and compliance.

All dispute operations are managed independently - administrators can search, filter, and resolve disputes regardless of the associated payment or customer context.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_payment_id
foreignFields.description: Associated payment transaction being disputed. {@link shopping_mall_payments.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who initiated the dispute. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller against whom the dispute is filed. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator assigned to resolve this dispute. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: dispute_status
plainFields.description: Current status of the dispute. Valid values: open, under_review, resolved, cancelled. Status transitions follow dispute workflow rules.

plainFields.name: dispute_reason
plainFields.description: Category of dispute reason as defined by system standards (e.g., unauthorized_charge, goods_not_received, incorrect_amount, duplicate_charge).

plainFields.name: dispute_description
plainFields.description: Detailed textual description of the dispute issue, including timeline, evidence references, and customer claims.

plainFields.name: evidence_url
plainFields.description: URL to external evidence (e.g., delivery confirmation, transaction receipt, communication logs) uploaded by dispute party.

plainFields.name: resolution_notes
plainFields.description: Final resolution notes and decisions made by the assigned administrator.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the dispute was filed.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last status update or information update to this dispute.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this dispute record was soft-deleted (for audit purposes). Null if still active.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_vault_entries
models.description:
Encrypted storage of sensitive payment data for PCI-DSS compliant handling, never storing full PANs or CVVs.

Maintains encrypted payment tokenization records for saved payment methods that customers have explicitly consented to store. This table serves as a secure vault for payment credentials, ensuring compliance with PCI-DSS standards by never storing raw card numbers or CVV codes.

Each entry is linked to a specific customer and payment method type. The encrypted_data field contains encrypted tokenized values that can be decrypted by the payment system's secure key management service when initiating transactions.

Access to this data is strictly controlled by internal service layer logic - customer or seller UIs never directly access vault entries. All operations occur through payment processing system APIs.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who owns this payment credential. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_payment_method_id
foreignFields.description: Type of payment method this vault entry stores (credit card, PayPal, etc.). {@link shopping_mall_payment_methods.id}.

plainFields.name: encrypted_data
plainFields.description: AES-256 encrypted payload containing masked card number, expiry date, and payment token. Never contains full PAN or CVV as required by PCI-DSS.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this vault entry was created and stored in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this vault entry was last modified (e.g., when masked data was updated).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this vault entry was logically deleted (soft delete). Null if still active.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_exchange_rates
models.description:
Historical currency conversion rates locked at transaction time for accurate financial reconciliation.

Records official exchange rates used during payment processing, capturing the exact rate applied at the moment of transaction. These rates are immutable historical records, never updated after creation, to ensure audit-trail integrity for financial reporting and reconciliation.

Each entry represents a specific rate between two currencies as obtained from a designated external API source. The system locks these rates when a payment is processed, ensuring that the rate used for financial calculations remains unchanged even if market rates fluctuate later.

This table serves as the authoritative source for historical currency conversion values, critical for accounting, tax calculations, and financial audits that require precise, unaltered transaction data.

plainFields.name: from_currency
plainFields.description: The base currency code (ISO 4217) being converted from. Examples: 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY'. This represents the currency of the original transaction amount.

plainFields.name: to_currency
plainFields.description: The target currency code (ISO 4217) being converted to. Examples: 'USD', 'EUR', 'JPY'. This represents the currency into which the original amount was converted for the payment.

plainFields.name: exchange_rate
plainFields.description: The exchange rate used for conversion. Represents how much of the to_currency equals one unit of from_currency. For example, if 1 USD = 1.2 EUR, then exchange_rate = 1.2. Stored as a double for precise financial calculations.

plainFields.name: source_api
plainFields.description: The external financial API provider that supplied this exchange rate. Examples: 'fixer.io', 'openexchangerates.org', 'currencyapi.com'. Used for audit trail and to trace the source of rate data in case of disputes or quality issues.

plainFields.name: locked_at
plainFields.description: The precise timestamp when this exchange rate was locked for use in a payment transaction. This is the critical point-in-time reference for financial reconciliation. The rate at this exact moment is what was used in the payment calculation and must remain unchanged forever.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this exchange rate record was stored in the system. Indicates when the rate was fetched and persisted by the system. For audit purposes to determine how recently the rate was recorded.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this exchange rate record was last modified. In this immutable rate table, this field is set identical to created_at since rates are never updated after creation. Included for schema consistency with other tables.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_surcharge_rules
models.description:
Defines permitted surcharge amounts for specific payment methods by region, compliant with legal restrictions.

Stores configuration rules that specify how much additional fee can be applied to transactions based on the payment method and geographic region. These rules are used during payment processing to automatically calculate applicable surcharges while ensuring compliance with regional laws that restrict or prohibit certain surcharges.

Each rule applies to a specific payment method (e.g., credit card, digital wallet) in a specific country or region. The surcharge amount is stored as a decimal value representing the percentage or flat fee that can be added. Rules have effective dates to support historical tracking and future-dated policy changes.

foreignFields.name: payment_method_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the payment method this surcharge rule applies to. {@link shopping_mall_payment_methods.id}.

foreignFields.name: region_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the region this surcharge rule applies to. {@link shopping_mall_payment_regions.id}.

plainFields.name: surcharge_amount
plainFields.description: The amount of surcharge that can be applied, expressed as a decimal percentage or flat fee. Positive values only, representing the surcharge against the transaction amount.

plainFields.name: effective_date
plainFields.description: The date and time when this surcharge rule becomes effective. Used for managing future-dated policy changes and historical rule tracking.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this surcharge rule was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this surcharge rule was last modified.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_rate_limits
models.description:
Tracks payment attempt rate limits per user and IP address to prevent abuse and brute force attacks.

This subsidiary table automatically monitors and enforces rate limits on payment operations by counting attempts made by authenticated users and anonymous IPs. Records expire after a configured time window and are automatically cleaned up, making this a transient tracking system without long-term retention requirements.

The system counts attempts per user (when authenticated) and per IP address (when anonymous), triggering system-level blocks when thresholds are exceeded. This supports the payment-processing.md requirement for rate limit enforcement without exposing internal thresholds to users or requiring direct management.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Identifies the authenticated user making payment attempts. This field is null for anonymous users attempting payments. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}, {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}, or {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: The client IP address making the payment attempt. This field is populated for anonymous users and for tracking purposes even with authenticated users.

plainFields.name: attempts
plainFields.description: The number of payment attempts recorded within the current time window. Resets upon expiration.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this rate limit record was first created. Used for determining the time window.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this rate limit record will expire and be considered stale. After this point, the attempt counter resets.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_notifications
models.description:
Stores message templates and delivery logs for payment status notifications sent to customers via email and in-app alerts.

Records all system-generated notifications triggered by payment events including payment success, failure, refunds, and status changes. This table maintains an immutable audit trail of customer communications for compliance and support purposes.

Each record captures the notification template used, delivery method (email or app), recipient identifier, delivery status, and timestamps for when notifications were sent and read. External systems can query this table to verify communication occurred without exposing the actual message content to the API layer.

plainFields.name: template
plainFields.description: Identifier of the message template used for this notification (e.g., 'payment_success', 'refund_processed'). Reference to system-defined notification templates.

plainFields.name: notification_type
plainFields.description: Channel type used to deliver the notification: 'email' or 'app'. Defines the delivery method and routing logic.

plainFields.name: recipient_id
plainFields.description: Identifier of the recipient (customer or seller) who received the notification. Links to customer_id or seller_id in Actors component.

plainFields.name: recipient_type
plainFields.description: Type of recipient: 'customer' or 'seller'. Distinguishes notification target within the Actors component.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Delivery status of the notification: 'sent', 'delivered', 'open', 'failed'. Tracks status through notification pipeline.

plainFields.name: sent_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the notification was dispatched to the delivery system (email gateway or push notification service).

plainFields.name: read_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the recipient opened or viewed the notification in the app or email client. NULL if never opened.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this notification record was created in the database.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this notification record was last updated, typically when status changes to 'delivered' or 'open'.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_settings
models.description:
System-wide configuration for payment processing behavior including timeout values, retry policies, SLA thresholds, and admin-controlled feature flags.

This singleton configuration table controls global payment system behavior across the entire platform. It determines how the system handles payment timeouts, retry attempts, service level requirements, and which payment methods are enabled or disabled. Administrators use the admin dashboard to modify these settings, which take immediate effect system-wide.

Each configuration change is tracked through the created_at/updated_at/deleted_at temporal fields to maintain an audit trail of payment policy evolution. This table does not represent any business entity but rather the operational parameters controlling how payment transactions are processed.

plainFields.name: payment_timeout_seconds
plainFields.description: Maximum time in seconds that a payment authorization request will wait for gateway response before timing out. Default: 30 seconds.

plainFields.name: max_retry_attempts
plainFields.description: Maximum number of retry attempts for failed payment transactions before marking as declined. Default: 3 attempts.

plainFields.name: sla_threshold_minutes
plainFields.description: Service Level Agreement threshold in minutes for payment processing completion. If processing exceeds this time, monitoring alerts are triggered. Default: 15 minutes.

plainFields.name: disable_card_payments
plainFields.description: Flag to disable all card-based payment methods (credit/debit) system-wide. When true, card payments are not available for any customer.

plainFields.name: disable_wallet_payments
plainFields.description: Flag to disable digital wallet payments (e.g. Apple Pay, Google Pay) system-wide. When true, wallet payments are not available for any customer.

plainFields.name: disable_crypto_payments
plainFields.description: Flag to disable cryptocurrency payments system-wide. When true, blockchain-based payments are not available for any customer.

plainFields.name: enable_surcharge
plainFields.description: Flag to enable payment surcharges for specific payment methods as defined in shopping_mall_payment_surcharge_rules table.

plainFields.name: enable_rate_limiting
plainFields.description: Flag to enable rate limiting on payment attempts per user and IP address to prevent abuse or brute force attacks.

plainFields.name: enable_webhooks
plainFields.description: Flag to enable webhook notifications to external systems for real-time payment status updates.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was logically deleted (soft delete), allowing audit trail of configuration changes.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_cryptocurrency_conversions
models.description:
Records blockchain-based cryptocurrency payment conversions with locked exchange rates at transaction time.

Captures the exact fiat currency amount received after cryptocurrency conversion, using the exchange rate that was locked at the moment of payment authorization. This ensures precise financial reconciliation despite exchange rate volatility. Each record corresponds to exactly one payment transaction and is automatically created when a cryptocurrency payment is processed.

Tracks whether the customer explicitly confirmed the conversion amount before completing the payment. Records the final settlement outcome (success, failed, disputed) for accounting reconciliation. This table provides immutable audit trail for crypto payments, fulfilling regulatory compliance requirements for financial reporting and dispute resolution.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_payment_id
foreignFields.description: The payment transaction this conversion record belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_payments.id}.

plainFields.name: fiat_amount
plainFields.description: The equivalent fiat amount (in USD) received from the cryptocurrency conversion, locked at the time of payment authorization.

plainFields.name: locked_exchange_rate
plainFields.description: The exchange rate (cryptocurrency per USD) that was locked at the time of payment authorization. This ensures financial accuracy despite market fluctuations.

plainFields.name: customer_confirmed
plainFields.description: Whether the customer explicitly confirmed the conversion amount and rate before completing the cryptocurrency payment transaction.

plainFields.name: settlement_outcome
plainFields.description: The final settlement status of this cryptocurrency conversion. Possible values: 'settled', 'failed', 'disputed'. Records the outcome for accounting reconciliation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cryptocurrency conversion record was created by the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was last updated (typically when settlement_outcome changes).

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_webhooks
models.description:
Tracks external webhook endpoints registered to receive real-time payment status updates from the system.

Stores configuration for third-party systems that require asynchronous notifications about payment events such as authorization, capture, refund, or failure. These endpoints are automatically triggered by payment status changes and are managed by system administrators through the payment settings interface.

Each webhook represents a specific URL endpoint that receives HTTP POST requests with payment event payloads. The system tracks delivery status, retry attempts, and failures to ensure reliable event delivery. Webhooks are associated with specific event types for targeted notifications and are subject to delivery health monitoring.

Soft deletion is supported to maintain audit trails while allowing configuration cleanup.

System-managed entity that supports payment processing but does not require direct user interaction or independent API operations beyond administrative configuration.

plainFields.name: url
plainFields.description: The complete HTTPS endpoint URL where payment events will be delivered as HTTP POST requests. Must be a valid, publicly accessible URL.

plainFields.name: event_types
plainFields.description: JSON array string containing the payment event types this webhook subscribes to. Valid values: 'payment_created', 'payment_authorized', 'payment_captured', 'payment_refunded', 'payment_declined', 'payment_dispute_opened', 'payment_dispute_closed'.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the webhook endpoint. Valid values: 'active', 'inactive', 'error', 'disabled'. Determines if delivery attempts will be made.

plainFields.name: delivery_count
plainFields.description: Total number of delivery attempts made to this webhook endpoint since its creation. Increments with each attempt regardless of success or failure.

plainFields.name: last_delivery_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent delivery attempt to this webhook. This helps monitor endpoint health and recency of activity.

plainFields.name: last_failure_reason
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of the most recent delivery failure reason (e.g., 'HTTP 500: Server Error', 'Connection timeout after 10s', 'SSL certificate expired').

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this webhook configuration was initially registered in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this webhook configuration (e.g., status change, URL update, event type modification).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this webhook configuration was marked for deletion, enabling soft delete functionality for audit trail preservation. If null, webhook is still active.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_batch_job_logs
models.description:
Logs execution of daily background jobs for endpoint monitoring, backup, reconciliation, and key rotation.

Tracks automated system processes that maintain payment system health, including monitoring checks, security key rotations, reconciliation procedures, and backup operations. Each entry represents a complete job execution instance with its outcome and diagnostic details.

This table supports operational visibility for system administrators by recording what jobs ran, when, how long they took, and whether they succeeded or failed with any error details.

plainFields.name: job_type
plainFields.description: Type of batch job executed. Valid values: 'monitoring', 'backup', 'reconciliation', 'key_rotation', 'data_cleanup'. Specifies the operational category of the background job.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Execution status of the job. Valid values: 'success', 'failed', 'partial_success', 'cancelled'. Indicates the final outcome of the batch job execution.

plainFields.name: job_duration_ms
plainFields.description: Duration of the job execution in milliseconds. Measures performance and helps identify slow operations requiring optimization.

plainFields.name: error_message
plainFields.description: Detailed error message if the job failed. Contains error codes, stack traces, and diagnostic information to aid troubleshooting.

plainFields.name: metadata
plainFields.description: JSON-formatted metadata about the job execution context. Stores extensible information such as system variables, configuration versions, or process-specific parameters in structured format.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the job execution was logged. Records when the batch job completed and was recorded in the system for audit trail.

models.name: shopping_mall_carriers
models.description:
Represents shipping carriers that deliver orders, including name and service details.

Stores identity and service information for third-party logistics providers that handle order delivery from warehouse to customer. Each carrier has a unique name and service description that defines its delivery capabilities and characteristics.

This entity is referenced by shopping_mall_order_shipments to associate orders with specific carriers. Carrier data is maintained by platform administrators and not directly modified by end users.

Common carriers include FedEx, UPS, DHL, and USPS. Service details may include delivery speed tiers, coverage areas, dimensional weight rules, and API integration endpoints.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Legal name of the shipping carrier (e.g., 'FedEx', 'UPS', 'DHL', 'USPS'). Must be unique across all carriers.

plainFields.name: service_details
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the carrier's service offerings, including delivery speed options, packaging requirements, tracking capabilities, and geographic coverage. Used to inform users during shipping method selection.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the carrier record was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the carrier record was last updated. Tracks administrative changes to carrier information.

models.name: shopping_mall_shipping_trackings
models.description:
Stores shipping tracking numbers assigned to orders by carriers.

Contains the unique tracking identifiers provided by carriers (FedEx, UPS, DHL, USPS) that allow customers and system to monitor the physical delivery status of shipments. Each tracking number is bound to a specific order shipment and can be used to query the carrier's API for real-time location and delivery updates. This table serves as the core reference point for delivery status tracking.

Tracking numbers are immutable once created and are never modified. Status changes are tracked in the shopping_mall_delivery_events table, which references this table via foreign key. This ensures data integrity and maintains an audit trail of order delivery progress.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_shipment_id
foreignFields.description: The order shipment this tracking number belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_order_shipments.id}.

plainFields.name: tracking_number
plainFields.description: The unique tracking identifier provided by the shipping carrier. This is the customer-facing number used to track the package through the carrier's system. Format varies by carrier (e.g., 1Z9999999999999999 for UPS, 999999999999 for FedEx).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this tracking record was created in the system. This represents when the carrier provided the tracking number and the system recorded it.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this tracking record was last updated in the system. This occurs when the tracking number is first created or if there are corrections to the carrier information.

models.name: shopping_mall_delivery_events
models.description:
Logs delivery status events received from shipping carriers for order shipments.

Tracks real-time status updates from carriers such as FedEx, UPS, DHL, and USPS at every milestone in the delivery process. Each event represents a single status change from the carrier system, providing an immutable audit trail of the shipment's journey.

This table is populated automatically by integration with carrier APIs and is never directly modified by users. Status values follow the order tracking workflow: "shipped", "in_transit", "out_for_delivery", and "delivered".

The notes field captures carrier-provided comments about delays, delivery attempts, or special conditions, enabling customer service teams to investigate delivery issues.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_shipment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the order shipment this delivery event belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_order_shipments.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current delivery status from carrier system. Valid values: 'shipped', 'in_transit', 'out_for_delivery', 'delivered'.

plainFields.name: status_time
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the carrier system reported this status update. This represents the actual time the event occurred in the carrier's system.

plainFields.name: carrier_update
plainFields.description: Raw status update text received from carrier API for this event, used for debugging and reference.

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description: Additional notes or comments provided by the carrier about this status update, such as delivery attempt details, package damage, or special instructions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: System timestamp when this delivery event record was created in our database.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_shipments
models.description:
Associates orders with specific carrier and tracking information for physical shipment management.

Captures critical logistics data linking orders to carriers, tracking numbers, and delivery expectations. This entity enables the shipping process by storing the connection between an order and its tracking details, allowing logistics teams, customer service, and customers to track shipment progress independently of the order system.

The tracking_number is a unique identifier assigned by the carrier that connects to carrier APIs for real-time status updates. The estimated_delivery_date represents the carrier's projected delivery date based on origin, destination, and service level. The actual_delivery_date is updated when the package is confirmed delivered.

This table is primary because logistics teams need to independently search, filter, and update shipment information without navigating through orders. It supports critical operations like: tracking specific shipments, updating tracking numbers, generating carrier reports, and identifying shipments with delivery delays.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: The order this shipment pertains to. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_carrier_id
foreignFields.description: The carrier responsible for this shipment. {@link shopping_mall_carriers.id}.

plainFields.name: tracking_number
plainFields.description: Unique tracking number assigned by the carrier for this shipment. This number is used to query carrier APIs for real-time delivery status updates.

plainFields.name: estimated_delivery_date
plainFields.description: The carrier's projected delivery date based on shipping method, origin, destination, and transit time. This value is typically populated when the package is handed off to the carrier.

plainFields.name: actual_delivery_date
plainFields.description: The date and time the shipment was confirmed delivered. Updated when the carrier provides final delivery confirmation.

plainFields.name: package_weight
plainFields.description: Weight of the package in kilograms. Used by carriers to calculate shipping rates and determine handling requirements.

plainFields.name: package_dimensions
plainFields.description: Dimensions of the package in format "length x width x height" (e.g., "30x20x15cm"). Required for carrier shipping rate calculations and handling specifications.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment record was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. When set, indicates this shipment record has been logically deleted but preserved for audit trail purposes.

models.name: shopping_mall_shipping_methods
models.description:
Configuration options for available shipping methods that customers can select during checkout.

Provides predefined shipping alternatives with associated delivery times and costs. These methods are referenced by order_shipments to identify which shipping service was chosen for a given order.

Shipping methods are configured by administrators and are not independently managed by customers. Customer selection occurs through order shipment creation, not through direct interaction with this table.

This table serves as reference data for the shipping subsystem, enabling consistent pricing and delivery expectations across orders.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Display name of the shipping method (e.g., 'Standard Ground', 'Express 2-Day'). Must be unique for clear customer identification.

plainFields.name: cost
plainFields.description: Fixed shipping cost in USD for this method. Zero is allowed for free shipping options. All values stored with exactly 2 decimal places for currency precision.

plainFields.name: estimated_delivery_days
plainFields.description: Estimated number of business days for delivery using this method after order processing. Used for delivery expectation management.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the shipping method's features, conditions, or restrictions (e.g., 'Available for orders over $50', 'Not available for international shipments').

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipping method was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipping method was last modified. Always updated on any change to record.

models.name: shopping_mall_reviews
models.description:
Stores customer reviews for products with ratings, text content, timestamps, and verification status.

Represents authentic user feedback on purchased products, serving as a community reputation system. Each review is tied to a specific product and created by an authenticated customer who has completed a purchase and received delivery confirmation.

Reviews must contain between 50-2000 characters of text and can include up to five supporting images. Customers can flag reviews as inappropriate, and moderators can approve or reject flagged content. The system prevents duplicate reviews from the same customer on the same product within a 7-day window.

Reviews are independently managed by users - customers can view their own reviews, edit or delete them (with moderation logs), and receive responses from sellers. The review rating system helps surface high-quality content through helpful/unhelpful voting mechanisms.

Review status tracks whether content has been approved, hidden, or deleted by moderation. The verification field confirms the reviewer completed a purchase and received the product before submitting feedback.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product being reviewed. {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who submitted the review. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current moderation status of the review. Valid values: pending, approved, hidden, deleted. Default is 'pending' for new reviews.

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: Numeric rating from 1-5 based on customer satisfaction. 1 is lowest, 5 is highest rating. This field directly captures the consumer's evaluation without requiring indirect calculation through vote count.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Optional short summary title for the review (up to 100 characters). Used for quick preview display.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Main content of the review with text between 50-2000 characters. Contains detailed feedback about the product experience.

plainFields.name: verified_purchase
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the review is from a verified purchase. Set to true only after confirmed delivery of the product.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was initially submitted.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was last modified, such as when edited by the customer or moderated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was soft-deleted by moderation or the user. Null indicates active review.

plainFields.name: vote_count
plainFields.description: Aggregate vote count based on customer feedback for the review. Count of helpful votes minus unhelpful votes. Initialized to 0 when review is created.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_votes
models.description:
Tracks helpful/unhelpful votes on reviews by other users to surface quality content.

Each vote represents a user's assessment of a review's usefulness. This system helps highlight valuable reviews and identify low-quality content through community moderation. All votes are tracked with absolute audit trails to maintain transparency and prevent abuse.

Votes can be cast by customers, sellers, or administrators who view a review. Once cast, votes can be changed or revoked by the user. The system prevents users from voting on their own reviews.

The vote type is fixed to either 'helpful' or 'unhelpful' and cannot be customized. Quality score calculations are performed in application layer or materialized views, not stored in this table to maintain 3NF compliance.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_review_id
foreignFields.description: The review being voted on. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer who cast this vote (if applicable). {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: The seller who cast this vote (if applicable). {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who cast this vote (if applicable). {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: vote_type
plainFields.description: The classification of the vote as either 'helpful' or 'unhelpful'. This standard value prevents subjective interpretations of voting intent.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the vote was initially cast. Invariant after creation to maintain audit integrity.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the vote was last modified (e.g., when a user changed their vote). Updated on every change to track recency.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_flags
models.description:
Records user-reported flags on reviews for moderation review, including reason codes and timestamps.

Each flag is created when a customer reports a review as inappropriate, triggering a moderation workflow. Flags are immutable audit records that capture the reason for reporting and the identity of the flagging user.

When a review accumulates 3 or more flags, it enters the moderation queue for review by platform moderators. Moderators then use the flag reason classifications to prioritize and resolve reports.

The flagging process does not modify the target review itself - the target review remains unchanged until a moderator takes action. This ensures review integrity while allowing community feedback.

Flag reasons are standardized to maintain consistency in moderation decisions, with options like 'spam', 'inappropriate_content', 'false_information', 'harassment', and 'other'.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_review_id
